siteMetadata.title: Joseph Crawford
siteMetadata.description: Software engineering, AI tools, and homebrewing — written by Joseph Crawford, a developer building web applications and making mead in Vermont.

frontmatter.title: Why Water Chemistry Matters for Mead
frontmatter.excerpt: Water chemistry is the key to consistent, balanced mead. Learn how dissolved minerals affect yeast health, must pH, perceived sweetness, and the Cl-SO4 ratio.

frontmatter.title: Bicarbonate: The pH Buffer
frontmatter.excerpt: Bicarbonate is the pH buffer keeping your mead must from crashing too acidic during fermentation. Learn how alkalinity prevents stalls and target 30-80 ppm.

frontmatter.title: Building Your Water Profile
frontmatter.excerpt: Learn how to build a complete water profile from distilled water for any mead style. Step-by-step salt calculations for one-gallon batches and four profiles.

frontmatter.title: Calcium: The Backbone Ion
frontmatter.excerpt: Calcium is the workhorse ion in mead, driving yeast health, flocculation, clarity, and mouthfeel. Learn why every batch needs 50-100 ppm and how to add it.

frontmatter.title: Chloride: Fullness and Roundness
frontmatter.excerpt: Chloride is the fullness ion that adds body, rounds harsh edges, and enhances perceived sweetness in mead. Learn target ranges of 50-150 ppm and when to use it.

frontmatter.title: How to Get Your Water Quality Report
frontmatter.excerpt: Learn how to find your local municipal water quality report or order a lab test when city data falls short. Covers EPA CCR searches and ions you must measure.

frontmatter.title: Magnesium: The Quiet Enabler
frontmatter.excerpt: Magnesium is a required yeast nutrient cofactor powering ATP production during fermentation. Learn the narrow 5-20 ppm window and adding it with Epsom salts.

frontmatter.title: Measuring pH: Meters and Calibration
frontmatter.excerpt: A digital pH meter is essential for mead fermentation stability between 3.2 and 4.2. Learn how to calibrate with buffers and which budget meters are worth it.

frontmatter.title: Sodium: The Sweetness Enhancer
frontmatter.excerpt: Sodium enhances perceived sweetness and rounds mouthfeel in mead, much like salt in caramel. Learn the tight 5-25 ppm target and when to skip it for dry meads.

frontmatter.title: Sulfate: Dryness and Crispness
frontmatter.excerpt: Sulfate is the crispness ion that dries the palate and sharpens fruit notes in mead. Learn target ranges of 50-150 ppm and when to use it for dry show meads.

frontmatter.title: Bottling
frontmatter.excerpt: Bottling is the final step before drinking your mead. Learn to pick swing-top or crown-cap bottles, still versus carbonated, priming, and sediment handling.

frontmatter.title: Fueling the Fermentation: Supporting the Brewing Journey
frontmatter.excerpt: Support my brewing experiments via Ko-fi. Contributions fund quality honey, specialized yeast, and rare fruit additions for detailed mead-making findings.

frontmatter.title: Pasteurization
frontmatter.excerpt: Pasteurize mead with heat to stop fermentation without chemical stabilizers. Bottle sweet or carbonated mead safely using the kettle-and-fermenter method.

frontmatter.title: Back Sweetening
frontmatter.excerpt: Back sweetening mead means adding honey after fermentation to balance sweetness. Learn to stabilize yeast first, then taste-test to a honey-forward finish.

frontmatter.title: Secondary Fermentation
frontmatter.excerpt: Discover why and when to rack mead into secondary fermentation, what happens during clearing and aging, and how to know when your mead is ready to bottle.

frontmatter.title: Primary Fermentation
frontmatter.excerpt: Primary fermentation is where yeast turns honey water into mead. Learn what happens during active fermentation, when to add fruit, and how to confirm it's done.

frontmatter.title: Mead Ingredients
frontmatter.excerpt: Mead is honey, water, and yeast, but your choices shape the glass. Learn honeys, yeast strains like Lalvin D-47 and EC-1118, nutrients, and key additions.

frontmatter.title: Preparing Your Must
frontmatter.excerpt: Learn how to prepare mead must by mixing honey and water, combining ingredients thoroughly, oxygenating, and taking an accurate original gravity reading.

frontmatter.title: Cleaning and Sanitization
frontmatter.excerpt: Cleaning and sanitizing are different jobs and both matter for mead. Learn why brewing is 80 percent cleaning and the routine I follow every brew day.

frontmatter.title: Equipment You Need
frontmatter.excerpt: A practical guide to mead brewing gear for your first one-gallon batch: fermenters, airlocks, auto-siphons, hydrometers, and the few tools worth buying first.

seriesCards.name: Mead Water Chemistry
seriesCards.description: A comprehensive guide to water chemistry for mead makers — from ion fundamentals to building custom water profiles for different mead styles.

seriesCards.name: Intro to Making Mead
seriesCards.description: A complete beginner's guide to making mead at home, from equipment and ingredients through fermentation, back-sweetening, pasteurization, and bottling.
